findings.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Resolve fixes relative to the nested project**

When `code_check` or `code_lint` receives a path inside an excluded/nested Rust project, `run_verify` executes Cargo in that project's subdirectory, so rustc reports paths such as `src/lib.rs` relative to that subdirectory. Passing the outer checkout root to `plan` makes these fixes resolve as `<checkout>/src/lib.rs`; they are therefore skipped, or can be applied to an unrelated outer file if one exists and passes the line check. Resolve edits relative to the project directory selected by `engine_project`, while retaining the outer root for the workspace-boundary check.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

evidence.explanation: Fixes retain compiler-relative filenames while only diagnostics get nested subdir prefix; plan still receives checkout root.
evidence.verification: Source trace only; public reproduction assigned before edits. Semantic outline refused due capacity; bounded exact reads used.

findings.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Normalize paths before accepting workspace fixes**

For a module loaded with a path such as `#[path = "../../outside.rs"]`, rustc preserves a diagnostic filename like `src/../../outside.rs`. This check accepts it because it is neither absolute nor prefixed by `..`, and `root.join(...)` can point to an existing file outside the checkout; the later workspace-edit guard then rejects the URI and aborts the entire `--fix` call instead of recording this suggestion as skipped, preventing valid in-workspace fixes from being applied too. Canonicalize or component-normalize each path and verify it remains under the canonical workspace root here.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

evidence.explanation: Raw prefix check accepts internal parent components and symlink escapes before later workspace guard aborts application.

findings.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Propagate failures from the fixer command**

When the initial lint succeeds but the fix-mode invocation fails to start, times out, or exits nonzero before rewriting a file, this code ignores `outcome.exit` and leaves `after` unset. `Fixed::ok()` then falls back to the successful `before` report, so `code_lint` returns success and says that zero files were rewritten even though the requested fix command failed; validate and report the fixer exit status before deriving success from `pulled_files`.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

evidence.explanation: Tool fixer outcome exit is ignored; no pulled files means no after report, and Fixed::ok inherits successful before.
